summary: Coverage judge rm-coverage-judge-1793955968 returned not_covered with 5 gaps; gap 2 needs his answer (does his shock rule cover a sparking floor-cut end?), so the lock returns to stage 2; the other four are stage-3 scene fixes carried in the decision. Tree not signed.
decision: Whether his shock rule (s_shock_fix_safe: a fixer approaching a sparking line is safe, an incidental crosser is shocked) also covers the sparking live end a floor-conduit cut leaves (cut_live_and_dead_ends, the flagship), or only fallen overhead spans. Then stage 3 must fix the coverage gaps from coverage_verdict.json: (1, return_to 3) The fixer exemption is never tested against the obvious wrong way to build it: exempting anyone doing a re-string job. His words are 'if they approach intending to fix it', meaning that particular wire, and exam c3 says a colonist re-stringing a different span who crosses this live end must be shocked. sc_shock and sc_shock_restring only use a re-stringer assigned to this wire, and the shock_restring control just reassigns them to hauling. An exemption keyed on the job type (the leaf's oracle reads 'none on the re-stringer while on RM_RestringSpan') would pass every scene. Add a control case: a colonist on RM_RestringSpan for another span crosses this sparking end and is shocked. [scenes.json sc_shock / sc_shock_restring control; tree.json fallen_wire_shocks_crossers oracle_proposed]; (2, return_to 2) His root line says 'how a Pawn ever fixes a sparking line ... if they incidentally go over the sparking end with a different job, they (or anyone else) gets shocked'. A floor-conduit cut also leaves a sparking live end: cut_live_and_dead_ends, which is the flagship workshop-floor moment. The tree applies shock (and the fixer-is-safe rule) only to fallen overhead spans. No leaf says whether a sparking floor-cord end shocks a pawn crossing it, or whether a constructor rebuilding the cut conduit is safe. Whether his shock rule covers floor cut ends is a scope question about his own words, so it needs his answer, then a leaf and scene either way. [record.json root / scope s_shock_fix_safe; tree.json cut_live_and_dead_ends and fallen_wire_shocks_crossers; sheet.md does-list]; (3, return_to 3) statics_clear_between_games is defined as 'starts or loads another' game in the same session, but sc_statics_new_game only starts a second quicktest. Loading a save goes through a different init path, and that is the path where an old game's tap or style pick could leak. Add a load-a-save case, or a second game reached by loading. [scenes.json sc_statics_new_game; tree.json statics_clear_between_games experience]; (4, return_to 3) sc_settings does not assert the parts of settings_switch_cleanly that are specific to this leaf. Nothing checks that the master switch brings back vanilla LAMP art without a restart; sc_conduit_invisible and the walk check conduit art only. Nothing reads 'every Harmony patch maps to one switch'. Nothing checks that the pipe-pole switch 'leaves power poles alone': the expect says only that 'pipe poles follow only their own switch'. Name these three observations in the scene. [scenes.json sc_settings expect; tree.json settings_switch_cleanly oracle/experience]; (5, return_to 3) wire_down_alert, as built and in the restring_cut_span leaf, lists anchors with a cut OR grounded wire, jumps to the anchor, and clears on re-string. sc_restring only stages a cut span. It never checks the jump-to, and never checks the grounded case (a killed mast, as in sc_fallen_span). overhead_spans also names lamp masts, and sc_spans stages no lamp mast. These built parts are exercised by no scene. [scenes.json sc_restring, sc_spans; record.json inventory wire_down_alert, overhead_spans]
question: In the workshop-floor showcase, a cord is cut and its live end lies sparking on the floor. A hauler walks over that end on another job. Should they be shocked, as with a fallen overhead wire, and should the colonist rebuilding that cut conduit be safe, as the re-stringer is? Or is a sparking floor end only a look, harmless to touch? (1) Same rule as fallen wires: crossers shocked, the one fixing it safe. (2) Harmless: the spark is only drawn. Recommended: (1), since your words say 'the sparking end', not 'the fallen wire'.
